name: CH-05 Client Hunt - Send approved outreach

nodes.name: Every 5 minutes
nodes.notes: Sends at most ONE message per run. With the 5-minute minimum gap and the daily cap, the brake - not this schedule - decides how fast mail goes out.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: Sends on its own. Daily cap = min(max_per_day, warmup_start + warmup_step x days since the first send). max_per_day is 30 since 6 Oct 2026: published cold-email data puts the safe volume for one mailbox at about 30 a day while a domain is young, and replies peak at 20-49 a day per sender (Instantly, Hunter). More volume should come from a second mailbox, not from pushing this one to 100. from_name is who the mail is from in the inbox: a person at the company, so it reads as one-to-one - the owner's choice on 6 Oct 2026 (it was the company name before). max_bounces was 5 until 6 Oct 2026, when every first message started going through a Reoon mailbox check ("Is the mailbox real?"): the five bounces before that were all unchecked directory addresses, so the floor was raised to 8 to let checked mail resume; 3 more bounces with checking in place still stop everything.

parameters.query:
-- CH-05: what has the sender already done today, and how healthy is it?
--
-- Read BEFORE picking a message to send, so the brake can refuse before it
-- ever looks at a candidate - the same ordering as CH-01's spend check.

SELECT
  (SELECT count(*) FROM outreach
     -- Every message that LEFT today counts, whatever happened to it after:
     -- a bounce or a reply changes its status, not the fact that it was sent.
     -- Counting only status 'sent' let two bounces through a 20-a-day cap.
     WHERE status IN ('sent', 'replied', 'bounced')
       AND sent_at >= date_trunc('day', now()))                              AS sent_today,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM outreach WHERE status = 'sent')                    AS sent_total,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM outreach WHERE status = 'bounced')                 AS bounced_total,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM outreach WHERE status = 'bounced'
     AND coalesce(reply_at, sent_at) >= now() - interval '7 days')         AS bounced_7d,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM outreach WHERE status IN ('sent', 'replied', 'bounced')
     AND sent_at >= now() - interval '7 days')                            AS sent_7d,
  -- When the latest bounce came in: the brake's alarm speaks only right after
  -- a bounce, not every hour for the week a tripped brake stays tripped.
  (SELECT max(coalesce(reply_at, sent_at)) FROM outreach
     WHERE status = 'bounced')                                           AS last_bounced_at,
  (SELECT max(sent_at) FROM outreach WHERE sent_at IS NOT NULL)          AS last_sent_at,
  (SELECT min(sent_at) FROM outreach WHERE sent_at IS NOT NULL)          AS first_sent_at;

-- CH-05: the next message a human has approved to send.
--
-- Re-checks suppression and closure AT SEND TIME, not just at draft time -
-- the two can be minutes or weeks apart, and a suppression added after a
-- draft was approved must still stop the send. Restating every precondition
-- at the point of sending is deliberate, from the job-hunt project's own
-- brake: "it belongs here rather than only upstream: this is the last place
-- before an email leaves, so a mistake anywhere earlier still cannot produce
-- a second copy."

SELECT
  o.id, o.business_id, o.to_email, o.subject, o.body, o.sequence_step,
  b.name AS business_name, b.country_code, b.is_natural_person, b.permanently_closed,
  -- Where the address came from: the mailbox check trusts a catch-all domain
  -- only for an address printed on the business's own website.
  b.raw ->> 'email_source' AS email_source,
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM suppression sup
    WHERE (sup.kind = 'email' AND lower(sup.value) = lower(o.to_email))
       OR (sup.kind = 'place_id' AND sup.value = b.google_place_id)
  ) AS now_suppressed
FROM outreach o
JOIN businesses b ON b.id = o.business_id
WHERE o.status = 'approved'
-- Best leads first: with a daily cap, the order decides who hears from us
-- at all. Highest current lead score, then the longest-waiting.
ORDER BY (SELECT s.total FROM lead_scores s WHERE s.business_id = o.business_id
          ORDER BY s.scored_at DESC LIMIT 1) DESC NULLS LAST,
         o.approved_at ASC
LIMIT 25;

nodes.name: BRAKES: may we send this one?
Is the mailbox real?
nodes.notes: Reoon power-mode check of the address before the first message to it. Only 'send' goes on; a failed check sends nothing and leaves the message approved.

BCC goes to our own mailbox. SMTP never writes a copy into the Sent folder - only a mail client does - so without this, outbound mail is invisible in the inbox the replies arrive in. The copy arrives FROM our own address, which CH-06 ignores, so it can never be mistaken for a reply.
nodes.name: Send it

parameters.query:
-- CH-05: record that the send actually happened.
--
-- The WHERE clause repeats status = 'approved' on purpose. If this workflow
-- were somehow triggered twice at once - two manual clicks, or a schedule
-- added later without updating this guard - both executions would pick the
-- same "next approved message", but only the first UPDATE would find a
-- matching row; the second finds it already 'sent' and updates nothing. That
-- is the same idempotency guarantee CH-02's write-verdict.sql uses.

UPDATE outreach SET
  status  = 'sent',
  sent_at = now(),
  message_id = NULLIF($2, ''),
  -- What the mailbox check said ($3), so every send carries its proof.
  guard_flags = guard_flags || jsonb_build_object('mailbox_check', NULLIF($3::text, ''), 'mailbox_checked_at', now())
WHERE id = $1::bigint
  AND status = 'approved'
RETURNING id, sent_at;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [$('BRAKES: may we send this one?').first().json.id, $json.messageId || '', $('Is the mailbox real?').first().json.mailbox || ''] }}

parameters.query:
-- CH-05: the mailbox check said this one must not go.
--
-- $1 outreach id, $2 verdict ('hold' | 'drop'), $3 reason, $4 Reoon status.
-- 'hold' parks it for a human; 'drop' skips it and suppresses the address,
-- the same as a bounce would have - without the bounce. Any other verdict
-- (an 'error' - the check itself failed) changes nothing: the message stays
-- approved and is checked again next run.
-- status = 'approved' is repeated for the same reason mark-outreach-sent.sql
-- repeats it.

WITH changed AS (
  UPDATE outreach SET
    status        = CASE WHEN $2::text = 'drop' THEN 'skipped' ELSE 'needs_review' END,
    review_reason = $3::text,
    guard_flags   = guard_flags || jsonb_build_object('mailbox_check', $4::text, 'mailbox_checked_at', now())
  WHERE id = $1::bigint
    AND status = 'approved'
    AND $2::text IN ('hold', 'drop')
  RETURNING id, to_email, status
),

suppressed AS (
  INSERT INTO suppression (kind, value, reason)
  SELECT 'email', lower(to_email), 'mailbox check: ' || $4::text || ' on ' || to_char(now(), 'YYYY-MM-DD')
  FROM changed
  WHERE status = 'skipped'
  ON CONFLICT (kind, lower(value)) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING id
)

SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM changed) AS changed, (SELECT count(*) FROM suppressed) AS suppressed;

parameters.content:
## CH-05 — Send approved outreach

**Sends on its own, every 5 minutes - one message per run.** It sends the oldest row with `status = 'approved'`: CH-04 approves a draft automatically only when it passed every guard; anything held stays `needs_review` and is never sent unless a human approves it.

### The brake, every run

1. Bounce circuit breaker — 8 bounces in 7 days (or 8% of sends) stops everything.
2. Daily cap — 100/day (owner's instruction).
3. Every precondition re-checked at send time: suppression, closure, natural-person flag.
4. Minimum gap since the last send.
5. Not at the weekend, and inside business hours, in the **recipient's** country.
6. **Is the mailbox real?** — Reoon checks the address before the first message. Only a confirmed mailbox is sent; a dead one is skipped and suppressed, an unconfirmable one held for review, and a failed check sends nothing.

Every send is BCC'd to our own mailbox and reported on Telegram. CH-06 marks replies and bounces and stops the follow-up.

To stop all sending: unpublish this workflow, or set CH-04's `auto_approve` to false.
